issue.title: `gh pr list` with flags fails JSON parsing
issue.author: yrahul3910

summary.headline: Parallel gh processes corrupt the on-disk API cache, so filtered `gh pr list` fails to parse JSON
summary.tldr: `gh pr list --author` failed with `invalid character 'd' after object key` because a cached feature-detection response had been corrupted by two gh processes writing the same cache file. go-gh's cache truncated and rewrote files in place, guarded only by an in-process mutex. go-gh#263 made cache writes atomic (temp file + rename) and shipped in gh 2.101.0; entries already corrupted still need `gh config clear-cache` (self-healing proposed in go-gh#300, still open).

nodes.title: Filtered `gh pr list` fails with a JSON parse error
nodes.detail: `gh pr list --author "@me"` and `--search ...` print `invalid character 'd' after object key`; plain `gh pr list` works.

nodes.title: gh 2.100.0 on a repo the reporter says is GitHub Enterprise
nodes.detail: Reporter ran gh 2.100.0 (2026-09-03). They said the repo is on GitHub Enterprise, though the debug log shows requests to api.github.com.

nodes.title: Debug log shows a cached body starting with `{"{"data"`
nodes.detail: With `GH_DEBUG=api`, the second request (`SearchType_enumValues` introspection, `X-Gh-Cache-Ttl: 24h`) returns in ~460µs with an old `Date` header and a body with a duplicated prefix: `{"{"data":{"SearchType":...`.

nodes.title: Filter flags make `gh pr list` build or parse bad JSON
nodes.detail: The reporter's framing: the flags themselves break JSON parsing in `gh pr list`.

nodes.title: Triage: failure is in the cached feature-detection call
nodes.detail: Filter flags trigger GHES advanced-search feature detection, which is memoized in the on-disk HTTP cache (24h TTL). The live response before it is valid JSON; the cached one is not. Points at cache corruption from concurrent or interrupted writes, but could not confirm the mechanism.

nodes.title: `gh config clear-cache` makes the error go away
nodes.detail: Maintainer asked the reporter to clear the cache; the command then worked.

nodes.title: It was a one-off glitch; close the issue
nodes.detail: After clearing the cache fixed it, the reporter closed the issue as a one-off. The maintainer reopened it the next day, linking it to a known go-gh bug.

nodes.title: go-gh#252 reports the same error from a corrupted cache entry
nodes.detail: Another user hit `invalid character 'd' after object key` on `gh pr merge`, with a cached `PullRequest_fields` body containing an interleaved prefix `{"data":{"PullReque{"data":...`.

nodes.title: Concurrent gh processes corrupt the HTTP cache file
nodes.detail: Maintainer: "It's probably cli/go-gh#252" and notes gh is now often run in parallel (e.g. by agents).

nodes.title: Cache writes truncate the file in place with only an in-process lock
nodes.detail: go-gh's cache `store` truncated the existing file and wrote the new body. Its mutex only serializes writers inside one process, so two `gh` processes could interleave writes to the same entry (or a crash could leave a partial file). The corrupted entry kept valid HTTP framing, so it was served for up to 24h.

nodes.title: Run `gh config clear-cache`
nodes.detail: Removes corrupted entries. Still the only cure for entries corrupted before the fix.

nodes.title: go-gh#263: write cache entries to a temp file, then rename
nodes.detail: Makes cache publication atomic; failed writes leave the old entry untouched; retries Windows sharing conflicts. Fixes go-gh#252. Approved by niik.

nodes.title: cli#14461 bumps go-gh to v2.16.1, which includes #263
Fix shipped in gh v2.101.0; issue closed as completed
nodes.detail: The v2.101.0 release notes list the go-gh bump. Nobody on the thread reported re-testing; the maintainer closed the issue on 2026-10-09.

nodes.title: Entries corrupted before the fix are still served
nodes.detail: Pointed out by LucasLeao18; go-gh#300 proposes a SHA-256 sidecar that evicts bad entries. Still open and unreviewed at analysis time.

edges.note: Live request is valid; only the cached feature-detection body is malformed
Same corruption seen independently on another command
Pulls the go-gh fix into gh
Atomic writes do not heal entries already corrupted

open_questions: Will go-gh#300 (integrity check and eviction) be merged so already-corrupted entries self-heal?
The reporter never confirmed the fix on 2.101.0 or later.
next_steps: Review go-gh#300 and bump go-gh in cli/cli once it lands.
Until then, document `gh config clear-cache` for users on pre-2.101.0 caches.
